script_defect_found.summary: check_archive() assumed digests.lock's image_id (docker inspect .Id at collection time) always equals the docker-save archive's manifest.json Config digest. Under Docker Desktop's containerd-backed image store (default since 4.34, active on this machine), .Id returns the pulled manifest(-list) digest instead.
script_defect_found.first_fix_bypassable: The first fix (e151d11) accepted any index.json manifest digest whose blob re-hashed correctly, but nothing linked that blob to the manifest.json Config/Layers syft actually scans; an approval review's PoC tar (real index bytes + unrelated manifest.json/config) was accepted. The classic path also never checked layer tars against the config's rootfs.diff_ids.
script_defect_found.fix: scripts/airgap/archive_identity.py check_archive(): every manifest.json layer is re-hashed (stored bytes, and gzip-decompressed stream) and must equal config rootfs.diff_ids in order; if the lock digest is the config digest that is the whole binding (classic). Otherwise the lock digest must be a blob in the archive that re-hashes to its name; a manifest list selects exactly one linux/arm64 entry (ambiguity rejected), that manifest blob is re-hashed, its config.digest must equal the re-hashed manifest.json Config and its layers[].digest must equal the re-hashed manifest.json Layers blobs in order. index.json is never consulted. Tar members with traversal, links, or duplicate names are rejected.
script_defect_found.regression_tests_added: scripts/airgap/test_archive_identity.py (run by test_sbom.sh): 5 genuine chains accepted, 15 forged/malformed archives rejected (reviewer PoC, swapped/reordered layers, rewritten config, mismatched config, two linux/arm64 manifests, missing list/manifest/layer blob, manifest blob not hashing to its name, unrelated lock digest, classic layer swap, path traversal, symlink, duplicate manifest.json).

regenerated_note: SPDX files were regenerated after archive_identity.py's resource-exhaustion caps and per-path linux/arm64 platform enforcement (third fix, critic review of the containerd-store fix above): syft output differs only in creation timestamps/namespaces, so sbom_sha256 values changed while per-image package counts and licenses.json are unchanged. All 12 real bundle archives are linux/arm64 and none exceed the caps, so none were newly rejected.

resource_and_platform_hardening.summary: Critic review of the containerd-store fix (check_archive() above) found two gaps: gzip layer decompression and whole-member JSON reads (manifest.json/config/index blobs) had no size bound, and the linux/arm64 platform check ran only on the manifest-list path, so an amd64 image locked by config digest (classic) or by a direct single-manifest digest (no list) would have passed and gotten a "verified" SBOM.
resource_and_platform_hardening.fix: scripts/airgap/archive_identity.py: gzip layers are decompressed in bounded chunks (zlib max_length) with a running-total cap (KUBEMETAL_ARCHIVE_LAYER_CAP_BYTES, default 8 GiB); manifest.json/config/index JSON members are size-checked against their declared tar size before being read in full (KUBEMETAL_ARCHIVE_JSON_CAP_BYTES, default 16 MiB); tar member count is capped (KUBEMETAL_ARCHIVE_MEMBER_CAP, default 100000) via lazy iteration instead of getmembers(); and the image config's os/architecture/variant is checked once, before branching, so it covers every binding path (classic, manifest-list, direct single manifest) instead of only the list path.
resource_and_platform_hardening.regression_tests_added: scripts/airgap/test_archive_identity.py: a gzip-bomb layer rejected by the decompressed-size cap without decompressing it in full, an oversized manifest.json JSON member rejected by its declared size, and amd64 images rejected via both the classic (config-digest) and direct single-manifest-digest paths (arm64 passing on every path was already covered by the existing accept cases).
